how: A member proposes the school logo and later builders explicitly join the located attempt.
Calls gather participants around a school logo and renew requests when defenders need more hands.
A builder answers the located construction call with an unqualified offer to help.
Defenders report being outnumbered and a numerical disadvantage without visibly giving up the drawing.
Participants negotiate palette constraints, lettering, dimensions and border choices rather than adopting one settled picture immediately.
Builders report working on the border and later announce completion before continuing protection.
Participants circulate coordinates and templates and replace one template with a cleaner version.
Participants recruit spare accounts, troubleshoot bot targets, circulate joint scripts and teach console execution.
Automation is contested through the school honor code, rule compliance and rival interpretations of the social experiment.
One room cannot test the population claim, while local requests for voting and an interim organizer decision prevent treating this case as wholly undecided order.
An organizer provisionally fixes one design overnight and defers reconsideration rather than waiting for a completed vote.
Declaring the logo complete immediately creates a duty to protect it, clean intrusions and limit expansion.
Attribution names school rivals as attackers but also separates visiting collaborators from vandals they cannot keep together.
A participant identifies a misclick and script operators identify incompatible friendly versions as sources of changed pixels.
Defenders allocate attention across their own logo, a state flag and other works whose repair needs differ.
Visitors and builders negotiate buffers, row trades and conditional ceasefires, with some offers accepted and others rejected.
A border request receives an agreement to lower the banner and an apology, followed by the neighbor's thanks.
Members alternate repair targets, solicit outside reinforcements and request help rebuilding another group's work.
Cross-school help includes reluctant assistance, conditional exchanges and later explicit gratitude.
An organizer explicitly celebrates an alliance with the neighboring rival school.
A member relays a collaboration offer from another school and asks a third neighbor to help that school.
Announcing a bargain does not establish compliance when continued attacks are reported and visitors disown unaffiliated vandals.
Apologizing for uncontrolled vandals and reporting a failed bargain do not explicitly dispute who is entitled to commit the room.
Negotiating adjacent space and borders does not establish that one school governs the other's work as its host.
Scattered initial attempts and later coordinates do not establish an erased work followed by a collective relocation decision.
School rivalry supplies the names used for attackers and the hostility directed at them.
Members invoke their existing school honor code to judge automation rather than merely choosing canvas colors.
Rule compliance does not settle legitimacy when members judge automation through an existing honor code and the event's social purpose.
Calling a moderator joke fun does not establish a host-wide April Fools takeover or general licence to treat canvas calls as fakes.
The coded moderator dispute identifies a reputational objection but does not establish a posting rule, megathread or removal policy.

statement: Holding a moderator's playful participation to the standards of the moderator role
how: A member rebukes a moderator's joke while the moderator defends it as fun, creating role accountability that canvas posting boundaries do not capture.
Participants declare accomplishment, recount repair labor and credit an organizer after placement ends.
Participants request a completion screenshot and mourn the temporary event.
Celebration, credit and sadness do not show a decision to continue the group or reuse the drawing after the event.
A criticism of scripts after closure contests participation's purpose without identifying a preserved version, cleanup or corrective historical account.
A participant proposes converting another flag, while a ceasefire explicitly exchanges help against a third group's work.
Rivalry is carried through taunts, accusations of vandalism and condemnation of the other school's sportsmanship.
Defensive school-rivalry language and proposed aggression are visible, but their concepts do not demonstrate a prior tie naming the target within the same attack call.
The located call receives offers of help and reports of construction, including an explicit switch from another attempt.
Starting and calling coincide in the first proposal rather than forming two demonstrably separate successive stages.
The same passage declares completion and immediately directs participants to protect the drawing.
Overwriting elicits an explicit offer to stop interfering in exchange for help building adjacent work.
A neighbor's border request receives a stated commitment to adjust and an apology, though subsequent pixel compliance remains outside this exchange.
A complaint about continuing vandalism receives a direct promise that a nearly finished bot will handle it.
Machine upkeep requires compatible targets because old and new scripts can undo one another and prompt a halt to changes.
Reports that construction is finished are themselves celebrated and later followed by explicit collective credit.
Recording can be requested prospectively before completion, so celebration is not a necessary preceding trigger.
A screenshot request and later mourning do not establish that recording generated a continuation decision.
Being outnumbered and moving between initial attempts do not establish that low manpower caused abandonment and relocation.
Templates can be revised while design remains disputed, so their circulation does not itself settle the agreed picture.
The construction call receives a bare offer to help without a requested return.
Another direct acceptance includes an account of prior work, fitting the model's allowance for acceptance beyond its ordinary bare form.
Help can be secured to stop a partner's attacks rather than simply to add hands against a shared threat.
A border exchange develops into a help request answered with a condition to respect the neighbor's northern boundary.
Aggressive proposals appear after mobilization but the concepts do not identify the call as their cause or demonstrate ensuing placements.
A proposed flag conversion and a ceasefire against another work lack a coded direct refusal or apology responding to those specific attack calls.
A negotiated ceasefire recruits aggression against a third party, so bargaining can generate an attack obligation rather than replace an attack.
Rivalry accusations and an orange-color threat do not establish that a locally issued attack call caused the contest in talk.
The alliance joins former attackers through conditional coexistence and shared scripts rather than demonstrating a common external enemy.
Mobilization and a later moderator-role dispute do not establish that a flood caused formal containment of canvas talk.
The bargain's reported breach and the visitor's apology establish compliance limits without an explicit subsequent dispute over representative authority.
Cooperating neighbors extend help into a combined drawing script when a participant asks to include both works in the same automated target.
